Original Requirements: Generate a complete medium-size Python 3.10 repository architecture for: Brick breaker game.
Testing Constraints: No manual interaction or GUI rendering
Cover runtime wiring plus one or two core rules
Language Convention Requirements: Python: keep Main.py thin and place reusable modules in a snake_case package.
Design an acyclic import graph; foundational modules must not import higher-level engines.
List pytest in requirements.txt and avoid non-essential dependencies.
Domain Reasoning: Core entities: Ball, Paddle, Brick, Level, Game state.
Rules: ball motion, wall/paddle/brick collisions, score and lives updates, brick durability/removal.
State transitions: level start, life lost, level cleared, game over/reset.
Configuration boundary via GameConfig owned by brick_breaker/config.py.

Import graph contract: config -> entities/level -> collision/game; brick_breaker/level.py uses from .config import GameConfig and must never import .game; brick_breaker/game.py uses from .config import GameConfig and may import make_grid_level from level.py; config imports no project modules.
Domain Expectations: Ball has position and velocity; updates per tick.
Paddle moves within bounds; user input abstracted as discrete left/right/no-op.
Collisions with walls invert velocity appropriately and clamp positions.
Paddle collision reflects ball with simple angle control based on hit offset.
Bricks have durability; on hit durability decrements and brick is removed at zero.
Score increases on brick destruction; lives decrement when ball exits bottom.
Level completion when all bricks are cleared; level reset on life loss if lives remain.
Game state encapsulates a tick(step) function applying input and physics deterministically.
Product Goals: Deliver correct, testable core mechanics with clean separation from runtime/UI.
Provide a minimal, deterministic automated test path.
Keep architecture small, coherent, and easy to maintain.
User Stories: As a user, I can move the paddle left or right and it stays within bounds.
As a user, I see bricks break and score increase when the ball hits them.
As a user, I lose a life when the ball falls below the paddle, and the level resets if lives remain.
As a user, I can complete a level by clearing all bricks.
As a user, I can start the program and see a small non-interactive demo step run safely.
Competitive Analysis: Classic Breakout (Atari): baseline mechanics with simple collision and scoring.
Arkanoid: advanced features such as power-ups and varied brick behaviors.
Pygame Breakout tutorials: common but often tightly coupled to rendering.
Minimal browser clones: easy to understand, often weakly structured.
Academic physics demos: precise but not game-focused.

Requirement Analysis: We must implement a Brick Breaker core with clean separation between domain logic and runtime/UI. The project must strictly preserve protocol files: requirements.txt (lists pytest), Main.py (thin entrypoint), and tests/test_main.py (single concise test target). The import graph must be acyclic and adhere to the FINAL NON-NEGOTIABLE checklist: brick_breaker/config.py is the sole owner of GameConfig; brick_breaker/level.py must literally use from .config import GameConfig and must never import .game; brick_breaker/game.py must literally use from .config import GameConfig and may import make_grid_level from level.py; config.py must import no project modules; brick_breaker/__init__.py re-exports GameConfig from .config. Domain logic includes ball motion, collisions with walls/paddle/bricks, brick durability/removal, score and lives, and level completion/reset. The runtime entry will run a small deterministic demo step with no loops or IO. Tests will cover public API only, asserting stable behavior such as a tick causing a brick break and score increment.
Requirement Pool: Preserve protocol-required files exactly (requirements.txt, Main.py, tests/test_main.py) and use pytest -q
Implement core mechanics: ball motion, paddle control, collisions, brick durability/removal, score and lives, level completion/reset

Enforce acyclic imports and the exact config/level/game ownership and import rules (from .config import GameConfig in level.py and game.py; level must never import .game; config imports no project modules)
Provide deterministic, headless tests covering runtime wiring and representative core rules
Keep files under 220 LOC and public API coherent across modules
UI / UX / Interaction Design draft: A simple 2D logical playfield with a paddle at the bottom, a ball, and a grid of bricks. Interaction (left/right/no-op) is abstracted into step inputs for deterministic updates. Main.py executes a small, non-interactive demo step that prints or returns a small status and exits. Tests avoid any real rendering or manual input and operate purely on the core API.
